contests.title: Hampton — homestead exemption after five years of residency

provenance.sourceOrg: Office of the Governor of Georgia
provenance.quote: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from City of Hampton ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes for the full assessed value of the homestead for residents of that city who have been residents for five years or more?

measures.questionText: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from City of Hampton ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes for the full assessed value of the homestead for residents of that city who have been residents for five years or more?

provenance.sourceOrg: Office of the Governor of Georgia
provenance.quote: Shall the Act be approved which provides a homestead exemption from City of Hampton ad valorem taxes for municipal purposes for the full assessed value of the homestead for residents of that city who have been residents for five years or more?

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Exempts the full assessed value of a qualifying homestead from Hampton city property taxes, including city bond taxes, beginning January 1, 2027 if voters approve. The resident must have maintained a primary residence in Hampton for at least five years, and the homestead may include no more than five contiguous acres. It replaces other city-tax homestead exemptions and does not apply to state, county or school property taxes. The resident or an agent must apply to the city or its designee, but residents who have applied for and received another city-tax homestead exemption for at least five years would receive this exemption automatically. The exemption renews while the home remains the resident’s homestead; recipients must report loss of eligibility.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the full city-tax homestead exemption for qualifying residents with at least five years of primary residency.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed full city-tax homestead exemption.
